question: Which peers does the turn-end comparison select for resynchronization, what does each peer present for a selection, and which fields feed the compared value?

scope.boundary: Static selection, notification, presentation and compared-field reads. Runtime policies, indices, delivery, load success and the first divergent field are outside it.

dependencies.use: Numeric case dispatch, case 55 and case 60 anchors, and the index-object consumer.
Snapshot queueing, stream receipt and the shared mode-1 loader that follow a selection.
Native label ImDoneAI for numeric type 53.

currentEvidence.method: Narrow generated-code windows and a lis/addi string-user scan over generated code, read independently twice. The canonical project's decompiler stops at save and restore thunks in these bodies, so generated code carries the claims.
currentEvidence.qualification: Only 0x82D8FCC8 materializes the three resync dialog and banner strings in the generated scan; dynamically sourced or duplicate text remains possible.

comparison.receipt: Case 53 ORs the sender bit into 0x83157E48 and stores its argument in 0x8312E5C0[sender].
comparison.gate: The body continues when 0x82D8AA60 reports the local peer as host and the receipt mask equals human mask 0x8312E608, or when 0x8314F1B0 is nonzero. That second condition can statically allow a non-host.
comparison.firstScan: 0x82CDE9B8 walks other connected humans that pass 0x82CD5A70, 0x82D8AB00, the 0x830ED0D8 flag, the 0x82D8F700 state, the city or settler tests and the 0x8314EF9F byte. A stored value differing from a fresh 0x82CD4CF0 result sets the predicate.
comparison.exchange: With the predicate set and halfword 0x82F77454 nonzero, the body clears 0x83157E40, submits type 55 at 0x82CDEAD0, and pumps 0x82E2A838 until 0x83157E40 equals the human mask. A failed pump leaves the loop, so older stored values can remain. Case 55 uses its scalar and seed only to set bit 0x10 of 0x82FFE7C4, then always replies type 60 with its index and a fresh scalar. Case 60 ORs the sender into 0x83157E40 and stores 0x8312E5C0[sender].
comparison.selection: 0x82CDEB44 takes a fresh local scalar and, for every index other than the local one that passes 0x82CD5A70 with 0x8312E5C0[i] different, builds an object with vtable 0x82136930 and +0x34 = i and passes it to service slot +0x44. The loop has no early exit, so one pass can select several peers. A seed mismatch does not select a peer.
comparison.routing: Service slot +0x44 resolves to 0x82CA6500, which attempts delivery to all present peer entries of 8, not only the selected index.

presentation.consumer: Object slot 0x82D91BD0 calls 0x82D8FCC8 with manager 0x8314EFDC and index +0x34.
presentation.selectedPeer: When the index equals the local index, 0x82D8FCC8 calls service slot +4 with zero (0x82CA5210) and UI virtual +0x234 with title 0x82136A64 and body 0x82136A34.
presentation.otherPeer: Otherwise it calls service slot +8 with the index (0x82CA51A8) and UI virtual +0x23C with banner 0x82136A74, naming the indexed peer through 0x82DAD4F8.
presentation.shared: Both branches then call 0x82D8F800 with state one and store 2 in the receiver +0x2C indexed entry. 0x82D8FE60 is the join variant and stores 1.
presentation.snapshot: 0x82D8FF78 queues a snapshot for each state-one index, moves it to state two, and selects banner 0x821369C8 or 0x821369E8 from the +0x2C entry. 0x82D8FB38 selects completion banner 0x82136ADC or 0x82136AFC for a non-local index.
presentation.reading: A peer's own selection shows the dialog and never its own name; another peer's selection shows a banner with that name and no dialog. A selection of several peers therefore shows each peer the dialog when selected, plus one banner for each other selected peer.

comparedFields.form: 0x82CD4CF0 returns a sum, so compensating changes can cancel.
comparedFields.units: 0x830F2BF0 + p*0x5400 + j*0x54, gated by owner +0 not 0xFF and +0xC bit 31 clear: j times signed type +1, signed X +0x1C, 2 times signed Y +0x1E, signed +0x52, signed rank +5.
comparedFields.players: For the count at 0x82F700AC: reserve 0x830ED544, culture strength 0x830ED4E4, derived culture level 0x830ED4C4, acquisition tally 0x830EDD08, strategy word 0x830E5250 + p*0x80, and when selected technology 0x830EDD48[p] is not -1, progress 0x830EDD68[p*48 + tech].
comparedFields.cities: 0x8314FE28 + j*0xBC for 128 entries, gated by owner +0 not -1 and population +3 above zero: owner, population, word +0x10, +0x34, +0x36, 2 times +0x38, +0x3C.
comparedFields.excluded: AI research lists and research progress other than the selected technology are not read.

guards: Comparison is against the comparing peer's scalar; a selection does not show which peer diverged.
Do not infer which peers were selected in a session, or their indices, from this static boundary.
A non-selected peer can still load through an independently available stream: 0x82D8F9A0 reaches 0x82D86400 through header +0x5C without an index test, with callers 0x82D217C8 and 0x82D8C820.
The consumption of a selection on the host is a premise, not a traced result.
Do not read a scalar difference as a named divergent field, delivery failure or true simulation divergence.
conclusion: The turn-end comparison selects every peer whose stored scalar differs from the comparing peer's, not only the first. Each peer sees the dialog for its own selection and a named banner for another peer's, so a named banner does not identify the only target. A runtime receipt is still needed for actual selections and the first divergent field.

nativeFirstDesyncDiagnosticHookBoundary.question: Where can a passive diagnostic observe the exact initial comparison, request and wait, reply writes and local command occurrence without inventing shared command or request identity?

evidence.method: Foreground read-only ghidra/DumpMemoryWords.java with radius zero, exact selected-word comparison against image.json, PowerPC decoding with Capstone 5.0.7, PE function extents and narrow generated instruction-comment corroboration.
evidence.qualification: The configured listing truncates these functions at known thunks. An instruction iterator that skipped to later listing entries was rejected. Selected memory words, not that iterator output, support these facts. One preceding exit-region word was byte-checked but not used in generated corroboration. There is no runtime observation or complete set of paths through the whole function.

nativeFirstDesyncDiagnosticHookBoundary.observationConvention: Each listed address denotes an observation before its original instruction. A scalar-return site is immediately after the stated native scalar call returns normally. Preserve the original instruction and guest register, condition and control state.

dispatcherOccurrence.normalExitView: r3 is the current return value and r1 is still the dispatcher frame before restoration.

nestingWord.meaning: The selected entry increments and common exit decrements this word. It is not a monotonic command ordinal. Other writers and non-normal exits are not closed.

dispatcherOccurrence.qualification: Selected case 53/55/60 normal exits reach the common exit. This is local invocation context, not proof of shared order, acceptance, application or a unique frame lifetime. Case labels in this record are inside the dispatcher function, not independent function entries.

initialComparison.qualification: The first scalar is preserved in r20 for the selected scan. Stored inequality alone does not set the final predicate: native filters remain. The fallback check can allow a non-host. Index helpers are sampled at their existing returns, not called again.

requestAndWait.pathSummary: A false initial predicate goes to the shared type-54 tail. With a true predicate and nonzero wait halfword, the selected path clears the reply mask, submits type 55, optionally pumps and scans for selection. With a true predicate and zero halfword, it submits type 55 without that mask clear, wait or selection scan, then reaches the same type-54 tail.
requestAndWait.qualification: Zero low byte from the pump reaches the join without the repeat mask reload. Log actual sampled mask comparisons separately from any observer-only current-memory read. The no-wait path has no mask-completion verdict. A later target consumer is not the original selector.

receiverAndReply.qualification: Capture arguments actually passed at the reply call. Do not infer r4 preservation across the intervening unexpanded helper or equate it to authenticated membership. Local receipt order and a cell write during a request interval do not prove causal request and reply matching.

beforeDispatcherCall.derivation: The immediately preceding instruction forms current frame +0x50.

localDrain.qualification: The consumer advances before copying and dispatching. A zero low-byte return takes a decrement path. The selected drain tail can reset both counters when the producer exceeds 0x40000000. These cursors are local and can roll back or reset. The copy-before-manager-callback observation is not automatically identical to later dispatcher inputs without preserved-frame and record conditions. Return status alone does not establish an applied gameplay command.

guards: All register roles are for selected normal paths and preserved readable native state. No runtime hook invocation, codegen preservation, non-normal cleanup, or which code holds, replaces and releases the reentrant observer was tested.

Incoming indices are raw values. These selected stores do not establish authenticated membership, a checked index bound or a safe unbounded diagnostic side table. Logging must preserve guest behavior.
Use frame identity only for internal correlation under a validated lifetime. Do not publish raw frame addresses or equate reuse of an address to reuse of one invocation.
A phase label identifies a static sample point. Equal phases, local counters, nesting words, ring cursors or turn numbers do not prove the same accepted command across PCs.
A native scalar return does not make a later reconstructed field ledger atomic. No first differing write or incident cause follows from these locations.

Existing title-injected guards and the code that holds, replaces and releases the observer require a separate pinned title-source integration check. They are not retail instructions and must not be overwritten by a diagnostic.
No new packet field, wire identifier, guest helper call, transport behavior, math or RNG change is part of this static result.
nativeFirstDesyncDiagnosticHookBoundary.conclusion: Exact selected instruction points expose native scalar phases, both receipt writers, actual mask comparisons and pump result, final selection operands and local drain and dispatcher occurrence. They support passive diagnostic proposals while shared command identity, causal reply matching, stable-world completion, atomic field capture and runtime safety remain not yet established.

nativeCommandContextBoundary.question: Does the selected command consumer preserve a separate occurrence tag from its network object, and what do its normal returns establish?

scope.qualification: Two complete bodies limited by their PE extents and one command-vtable consume cell only. Actual decoded object, current table and slot, supported ABI, valid preserved object, frame and record storage, normally returning callees and absence of destructive aliases or interfering writes are premises. No complete set of routing, factory, metadata-writer, transport or cross-PC ordering paths is claimed.

evidence.method: One serialized foreground read-only ghidra/DumpMemoryWords.java radius-zero query, exact comparison with image.json, Capstone 5.0.7 decode and narrow generated instruction-comment corroboration.
evidence.qualification: All 36 selected words equal the pinned image. The 31 body words match generated instruction comments. Extents are exclusive. Generated source is corroboration, not an installed binary or runtime evidence. Reused metadata-counter and receive contracts keep their own object, class and lifetime premises and do not prove the actual command takes every such route.

perObjectConsume.flagTest: 0x82CB1B40 loads incoming U+0x30 and 0x82CB1B44 compares the sampled byte. Nonzero skips the indirect call and returns the locally initialized zero. Zero selects U's current virtual slot +0x10 at 0x82CB1B5C with U as r3.
perObjectConsume.normalReturn: After that target returns normally, 0x82CB1B64 writes one to U+0x30 without a local success test. The wrapper preserves the target's raw r3 result. The object and field must remain valid through the callback and store.
perObjectConsume.qualification: This is a per-object flag, not proof of network duplicate rejection, once-only gameplay application or a persistent occurrence identity across reconstructed objects. A callback failure or non-normal exit or actual object lifetime is not closed.

commandConsumer.entryObject: Under the actual 0x821368E0 command-vtable premise, slot +0x10 selects 0x82D91C58. At 0x82D91C64 incoming r3 still denotes U. The original instruction changes it to U+0x34, and 0x82D91C68 requests 0x82CE16C8 with that embedded-record pointer.
commandConsumer.contextBoundary: The selected body does not read outer envelope fields or explicitly form a separate occurrence-tag argument. The accepted ring contract copies only type and four argument words. Other inherited register values are not assigned metadata semantics, and diagnostics may not recover an object by subtracting 0x34 from an arbitrary later record pointer.
commandConsumer.normalReturn: At 0x82D91C6C the queue helper's raw return is in r3. The next original instruction replaces it with one, which this body returns after its normal epilogue. Therefore the consume wrapper can mark U consumed and return one without establishing a newly appended, accepted or applied gameplay command. The accepted -1 record sentinel only drains existing work, and local dispatcher guards and retry paths preserve their separate meaning.

diagnosticCandidates.observation: Already sampled per-object byte in low8 r11 and preserved U in r31. Distinguish a skipped callback from a callback invocation without another flag read.
Actual current slot request with r3/r31=U and selected target in r10/CTR. Class and target and preserved storage must be established before reading candidate outer metadata.

The command-specific consumer still has U in r3 before forming the record pointer. A local object-to-invocation association, limited to the inspected scope, can start here, under actual entry, table and record and lifetime premises.
The actual record-pointer request has r3=U+0x34. Relate it to a checked local invocation, preserving the original call and guest state.
Raw queue-helper r3 before the original instruction overwrites it with one. Do not normalize it into gameplay acceptance.
Raw normal target return in r3 before the per-object flag store. This differs from queue-helper status when the selected target is the command consumer.

identityLimits: Five record words carry command type and arguments. No separate shared occurrence tag is in that record layout. Their equality alone cannot distinguish repeated identical command occurrences.

nativeCommandEnvelopeCounterBoundary ties together the selected command sender, current-info getter, constructor zero and modulo increment. nativeCommandRecipientHeaderBoundary proves, under conditions, preservation of the counter word during the selected recipient header write. Actual origin or info generation, complete transport or decode and matching command occurrence remain not yet established. The field remains supporting context rather than an accepted shared command key.
The selected lower transport uses connection-local 16-bit modular fields. They are not the five-word command record, an established cross-association identity or a proved global gameplay order.

Per-object consumed byte, local frame and observation ID, dispatcher depth, ring cursor, turn and load-attempt generation are distinct local observations. None alone establishes corresponding gameplay command occurrences across PCs.
nativeCommandContextBoundary.proposal: No behavioral title or SDK repair is selected. A passive diagnostic may preserve locally tied invocation and phase, actual record fields with validity and loss categories, plus checked object context at the command consumer. Repeated equal records remain separate observations. Any offline alignment depends on independently matched game and checkpoint, classified shared versus local work, compatible resets, supported nesting and complete coverage of the compared interval. A gap, unknown class or ambiguous repeated run must remain inconclusive rather than invent a shared sequence. Runtime observer composition, preservation and storage and callback lifetime remain UNRUN.
nativeCommandContextBoundary.remaining: Reuse nativeCommandEnvelopeCounterBoundary and nativeCommandRecipientHeaderBoundary for the candidate field's selected sender, constructor, receive and local header contracts. Actual sender namespace, complete capture and decode association, common gameplay order, causal replies and the first divergent field or write remain not yet established. These contracts do not close the broad online audit.

nativeCommandEnvelopeCounterBoundary.question: Can the existing object+0x28 counter identify the same gameplay command on different PCs?
nativeCommandEnvelopeCounterBoundary.classification: Partial. The selected normal command sender assigns the old current-info counter before serialization. The info constructor initializes that word to zero, and the selected envelope helpers include object+0x28. nativeCommandRecipientHeaderBoundary supplies the selected local header write's counter-preservation contract, which holds only under conditions. These facts support a correlation candidate, not a proved shared command key. Current sender and info generation, other counter writers, complete transport and decode and the dispatched occurrence remain unresolved. No incident cause or behavior fix was established.
nativeCommandEnvelopeCounterBoundary.scope: Eight selected functions contain 421 instructions: 150 reused and 271 newly queried. Two serialized foreground ReadOnly queries check 285 words, including 14 metadata words for seven PE extents. The pure getter is a complete two-instruction leaf without a PE row. Eight narrow generated windows corroborate the instructions at title 3f74e5f0995c4ebe6b0765b2ebe12d48ac85d6b7. Reuse prior command construction and dispatch, scalar-send, serialization primitive, lower-send and UI-independent receiver contracts. No further helper or global writer scan, project repair, game launch, service or behavior case was performed.
guards: Require the actual preserved sender S, current table, info I, message U, stack, buffer, descriptor and registry owners. The two info getter calls are separate samples. The first nonzero result does not establish the validity or identity of the second. Under the selected table, the pure getter returns U32[S+0x1C].

All reached objects and spans must be valid, mapped, compatible and preserved through use. Preserve normal ABI, nonvolatile, frame and FP returns, helper effects and disjoint storage. An explicit absence of a direct U+0x28 store is not a transitive no-write proof for callbacks, aliases or arbitrary current targets.

The actual constructor and factory, serializer and reader class, supported primitives and received route must be selected. The existing leading-value-77 factory-registration and delivery qualifications remain. Names such as service, descriptor, connection index and info do not establish authenticated peer, Civilization or world authority.

No global writer absence or reset-free lifetime is proved. Counter equality, one constructor zero, modulo arithmetic or equal local generation numbers cannot establish a common game, origin or command occurrence across PCs.
nativeCommandEnvelopeCounterBoundary.actualCommandSender: Reuse ai-options-boundaries.json#/findings/RVA-F-0362/commandDeliveryBoundary. The selected target=-1 submit slice constructs the command object with table 821368E0 and requests current child+0x44; cell 8215FABC selects CA6500 under the actual-table premise. The selected getter cell 8215FB80 chooses 82219D70. At CA6554 the sender reads U32[I+0x30]; CA655C stores the increment modulo 2^32 at I+0x30, and CA6560 stores the old value at U+0x28. It requests serialization once at CA658C before the index 0..7 fanout loop. It does not assign another U+0x28 value directly inside that loop. Per-recipient E465F8 and other helper effects remain separate, so a single pre-loop assignment alone does not prove identical final recipient bytes.
nativeCommandEnvelopeCounterBoundary.counterLifetime: I+0x30 is a four-byte counter, separate from U+0x30's consumed byte. The accepted CA2AB0 constructor writes zero at I+0x30 at CA2B28. Existing worldActorSessionInfoWriterBoundary ties selected CA5E80 allocation, construction and publication to S+0x1C, under successful compatible allocation, helper and owner preservation. A newly constructed info object therefore supplies a new zero origin under those conditions. The selected sender increments before its later S+0x14 presence test at CA6564..CA656C; that zero-field exit can consume a value without requesting serialization or fanout. Reuse nativeAdmissionScalarEnvelopeBoundary/headerCounterAndLowerCall: CA4F88 can increment the same info field for a different message class when the same actual sender and info mapping holds. Thus this field is not a count of successfully delivered gameplay commands. Modulo 2^32 wrap, reconstructed info and other writers prevent a universal uniqueness claim. No exhaustive reset or writer inventory is claimed.
nativeCommandEnvelopeCounterBoundary.envelopeField: The complete CB1F78 helper requests the accepted four-byte write primitive for U+0x28 at CB1FF8. The complete CB1EC8 helper requests the matching read primitive into U+0x28 at CB1F58. The field is the last word of the selected 32-byte base envelope. The read helper first compares the envelope version with 4; a mismatch requests a diagnostic, whose normal return would continue reading. This is not an unconditional rejection or a parser-safety proof. Supported compatible byte-order state, sufficient preserved buffers, normal primitive effects and correct class selection are necessary to carry the original numeric value across write and read. The selected methods do not put this field in the five-word command ring record.
nativeCommandEnvelopeCounterBoundary.receiveRouter: CA58A0 preserves U and samples U+8 for an accepted descriptor lookup. With a nonnull selected record it calls E463D0 using a separately returned current service+0x118 owner, U, a cached record+0x18 word and the incoming full mode. A nonzero low-byte return sets the local processing flag to zero and bypasses the remaining local delivery work. A zero return reaches a fresh service+0x118 and E46318 call. If that returns a zero low byte, CA5950 writes the then-current record+0x18 word to U+0x20 before a current service+0x128 call. The later path may request current+0x11C/E46108, then either C9F598 on the current info+8 object or current service+0xE0. It has no direct U+0x28 read or store. These requests are not completed processing or counter preservation through every helper.
nativeCommandEnvelopeCounterBoundary.validatorForwarding: E463D0 uses U32[incomingOwner+0x2C] for a fresh registry lookup. Under nonnull returned service, signed-nonnegative cached U+0x1C, a nonzero low-byte current+0x98 result and descriptor lookup, a nonnull record permits writing the supplied cached word at U+0x18 and requesting current returned-service+0x40 with U, record+0x14 and mode at E46474. Reuse nativeAdmissionSendBufferBoundary only when the actual returned table selects CA6448. That is the lower serializer, distinct from counter-stamping CA4F88/CA6500. E463D0 contains no direct U+0x28 store or counter increment. Its normal return 1 can also follow a null final record without a send request. CA58A0's nonzero-return suppression therefore does not prove forwarding, peer delivery or a command applied elsewhere.
nativeCommandEnvelopeCounterBoundary.validatorLocalHandling: E46318 independently resolves a registry service from incomingOwner+0x2C. It compares cached U+0x1C with the current service+0x7C result. Failure returns 0. After equality, signed-negative U+0x18 returns 1 without the selected store; otherwise it writes that U+0x18 value to U+0x20, performs current+0x100/CA9810 lookup and may request current+0x128 before writing the record+0x0C float. It returns 1 even when the record lookup returns null. This return selects a router branch, not successful gameplay. There is no direct U+0x28 store or counter increment in this body. The current registry service is not equated with the original sender or outer receiver.
nativeCommandEnvelopeCounterBoundary.identityConclusion: Proved statically: the selected command path uses a per-info modulo counter, with constructor zero, assignment before possible send exit, an envelope field and receive branches that depend on conditions. nativeCommandRecipientHeaderBoundary adds the selected recipient header write and counter-preservation conditions. Inferred: the field may correlate a particular serialized command if the actual sender generation, compatible complete capture and decode and consumption association are established. Unknown: a shared origin namespace, all reset or replacement writers, matching received command occurrence and cross-PC order. The counter alone is not a shared gameplay ordinal or proof of first divergence. Repeated values across info generations or wrap and gaps without delivery remain possible.
nativeCommandEnvelopeCounterBoundary.minimalProposal: No gameplay, title or SDK behavior change is selected. Do not add a new wire ID, reject duplicate counter values, require contiguous numbers or change counter resets based on this evidence. A default-off diagnostic can preserve the observed counter as supporting context, with explicit owner and generation and validity. Promote it to an occurrence key only after the required sender, header, decode and dispatch association is established. The existing local command transcript remains useful when this association is unavailable.
diagnostics: At CA6558 the actual old counter is already in r11, I in r3 and U in r28. Pair the counter store at CA655C with CA6560 and the U+0x28 store at CA6560 with CA6564. This distinguishes observed assignment from serialization, send request and delivery. Constructor CA2B28/CA2B2C supplies a local reset observation, bound to the existing S+0x1C publication rather than inferred from address reuse.

Pair envelope primitive requests CB1FF8/CB1FFC and CB1F58/CB1F5C with typed codec invocation and supported primitive result categories. Those call sites carry field pointers, not an already loaded counter value. Prefer a checked association with the primitive's actual value read or write. Reading U+0x28 afterward would be a separate diagnostic read within the inspected scope, requiring actual class, valid preserved extent and an explicit unavailable category.

Pair CA5908/CA590C, CA5938/CA593C and E46474/E46478 to separate validator results, a forwarding request and local processing suppression. Record the later C9F598 versus current+0xE0 request separately. A validator return 1 is not a send receipt.

Reuse the command-object hook point D91C64, record call D91C68 and helper result D91C6C. The consumer does not itself read U+0x28 and the ring copies no such field. Carry a checked local object and decoder association to that invocation, or specify one validated diagnostic read rather than claiming the guest supplied it. Preserve queue retry, reset, nesting and explicit losses. Use opaque local generations, reviewed numeric fields and validity only. Log no raw addresses, registry keys, identities, names or payloads, and add no clock, registry or service calls. No hook was implemented.
unrunCases: UNRUN: same preserved info versus reconstructed or replaced info, initial zero, modulo wrap, an interfering writer and different senders using equal counter values.

UNRUN: mismatch between the first and second getter samples, counter assignment followed by S+0x14 zero, other message classes sharing the counter, and send or serializer failure or no recipient. Counter gaps must not be classified as packet loss.
UNRUN: per-recipient E465F8 header changes, compatible codec states, insufficient or malformed input and a returned version diagnostic. The local helpers do not establish actual matching wire output.

UNRUN: E463D0 zero or one paths with present or absent final record, requested lower send, alternate current targets, E46318 comparison and signed-value paths, queued or direct processing and counter preservation across their helpers.

UNRUN: actual command class, preserved decoded object, same occurrence at the consumer, five-word queue copy, retry or rollback, snapshot replacement and cross-PC first-mismatch alignment. No command-key acceptance or incident cause is claimed.

evidence.method: Two foreground tools/run-headless.ps1 -ReadOnly DumpMemoryWords radius-0 queries. Every queried word equals the flat image. Capstone decode and eight narrow generated instruction-comment windows agree. Reused constructor range and ordered aggregate are independently matched; range digests derived from the aggregate are not relabelled as prior individual receipts.

aggregateReuse.qualification: The existing listed-order word set, including three cells and unexpanded neighboring command contexts, matches the aggregate exactly. Only the selected sender and getter ranges are interpreted here.

nativeCommandEnvelopeCounterBoundary.remaining: Reuse nativeCommandRecipientHeaderBoundary for E465F8's selected header effect rather than repeat the sender and router or generic buffer helpers. Actual info and origin generation, other counter and reset writers, full transport and decode and the processing occurrence still need their own evidence. A selected counter is not a world generation, recovery cutoff or shared command identity. The first differing gameplay field or write, paired samples, complete rejoin and other online families remain unresolved.

nativeCommandRecipientHeaderBoundary.question: Does the selected recipient header helper preserve the serialized command counter word?
nativeCommandRecipientHeaderBoundary.classification: Supported local write contract that holds only under conditions. E465F8 supplies a pointer to the low32 original index as the header helper's fourth-word input. The selected CB1BD0 path changes payload bytes at relative offsets 0x0C..0x10, not the counter at 0x1C..0x20. For the accepted fresh 52-byte command in the preserved 1450-byte buffer, it restores the counters and cursor to 52/Z+52. The selected later service+0x80 target and pure getter add no payload write under their class, span and preservation conditions. This does not prove actual recipient bytes, matching decode or consume, sender authority or a shared command key.
nativeCommandRecipientHeaderBoundary.scope: Four selected functions contain 168 reused instructions: E465F8, CB1BD0, CA4C90 and the two-instruction A73340 getter. One foreground ReadOnly DumpMemoryWords radius-0 query checks only three missing words: two E465F8 PE metadata words and one selected service+0x100 cell. Three PE extents and four narrow generated windows corroborate the selected code at title 3f74e5f0995c4ebe6b0765b2ebe12d48ac85d6b7. Preserve the original E465F8 and A73340 corridor hashes, which include eight and 47 excluded neighbor words. No new function body, generic buffer helper, route or writer scan was expanded. No runtime, game, SDK, service or behavior case was run.
guards: Preserve actual X, registry service J, selected table, buffer B, backing Z, caller homes, index slot, descriptor samples and stack. Require valid finite mapped disjoint spans, supported arithmetic, normal ABI, nonvolatile and frame returns and compatible helper effects without destructive aliases or replacement.

CAAAA8 lookup and E46518 eligibility preserve their accepted contracts and effects. They run before the header call. Absence of an explicit B argument is not proof that arbitrary callbacks cannot affect B. Whole-helper preservation requires their compatible noninterfering effects as well as the selected header contract.

For payload-footprint composition, B must use preserved 82136B28 methods and the accepted primitive, reset, relative-advance and snapshot targets. The accepted fresh command has 52 bytes in owned 1450-byte nonwrapping backing, zero callback and matching counters and cursor. Different classes, unsupported spans or callback, error or growth effects are not covered.

The returned service must actually preserve table 8215FA78 for the selected +0x80 and +0x100 associations. A registry lookup, similar field offsets or an earlier eligibility result does not prove that class or equate J with the original sender. No actual current owner or peer receipt is claimed.
nativeCommandRecipientHeaderBoundary.callerAndArguments: Reuse nativeCommandEnvelopeCounterBoundary and native-multiplayer-pause-input-delivery.json#/questions/3. CA6500 calls E465F8 with a separately obtained current+0x118 owner X, its buffer descriptor B and the current fanout index. E465F8 stores low32 incoming r5 in its caller-home slot at SP+0xA4. A null registry result or zero low byte from E46518 returns the preserved full original index without requesting the header helper.
